sub_indicators.label: Control of state data
sub_indicators.subject: geopol.sovereignty
sub_indicators.text: Digital sovereignty: control of state data
sub_indicators.norm_short: The AU Data Policy Framework asks for localisation of certain categories of data only, with portability so that no one is locked into a single provider; the Digital Transformation Strategy asks for 30 per cent of content hosted in Africa by 2030.
criteria: A source from the past three years says no policy or law governs where state data is held or who may process it.
The government adopted, published or announced a strategy, plan or draft rule to keep government data or systems under national control.
A law, decree or policy in force classifies government data or requires government or state data to be held in the country; a rule on personal data in general, banks or payment firms does not count.
With such a rule in force, government data or a core system is hosted in a government or nationally owned data centre or cloud in the country.
With stage 4 met, a government contract or agreement with a foreign provider or partner includes terms on data jurisdiction, portability, exit or handing over source code.

gaps.4: No source found since October 2023 says a government contract carries terms on data jurisdiction, portability or exit.
gaps.3: No source found since October 2023 says government data or a core system is hosted in a national data centre or cloud.
gaps.2: No source found since October 2023 says: is a rule on state data in force.
gaps.1: No source found since October 2023 says: is control of state data a stated goal.

ladder.empty: Nothing found says whether the state keeps its data and systems under its own control.
ladder.unplaced: Nothing found since October 2023 says whether control of state data is a stated goal or a rule.
